content.value_statement: Firestore setup can fail when rules, indexes, and SDK usage are planned separately. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create secure project files, validate access patterns, and guide Web SDK integration.
actual_capabilities: Creates Firebase configuration guidance for firestore.rules and firestore.indexes.json.
Explains secure Firestore Security Rules patterns with default deny and least privilege.
Reviews application queries to align rules with where, orderBy, and limit usage.
Shows Web Modular SDK patterns for reads, writes, transactions, realtime listeners, and queries.
Guides composite index decisions and field indexing exemptions for Standard Edition.
limitations: It does not replace a human security review before production launch.
It needs project-specific schemas and access requirements to generate accurate rules.
CLI deployment and emulator commands require local Firebase credentials and user approval.
Examples focus on the Web Modular SDK, not every Firebase platform SDK.

use_cases.title: Secure a new Firestore app
use_cases.description: Startup developers can create a locked-down baseline with rules, indexes, and SDK setup guidance.

use_cases.title: Audit app access patterns
use_cases.description: Security reviewers can compare queries, ownership rules, and validation checks before launch.

use_cases.title: Fix permission denied errors
use_cases.description: Frontend engineers can map failed Firestore operations to rules, indexes, or missing authentication.

prompt_templates.title: Create a locked-down setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me configure Cloud Firestore Standard Edition from a blank Firebase project. Include rules, indexes, and Web SDK setup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Write collection rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Firestore collections and write prototype Security Rules with validators for creates, updates, reads, and deletes.

prompt_templates.title: Match rules to queries
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan my app Firestore queries and explain which rules and indexes are needed for each access pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Harden and validate rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a threat review of these Firestore rules. Check ownership, schema validation, counters, PII exposure, indexes, and emulator test gaps.

output_examples.input: I have a new Firebase web app and need Firestore Standard Edition.
output_examples.output: A setup checklist covering Firebase configuration files, initial deny-all rules, index file creation, and local emulator testing.

output_examples.input: Users can edit posts, but only owners should change metadata.
output_examples.output: A rules design that separates owner updates from counter updates and protects immutable fields.

output_examples.input: My compound query fails with an index error.
output_examples.output: An explanation of the required composite index, when it is needed, and how to deploy it through Firebase tooling.

best_practices: Start with default deny rules, then add only verified access paths.
Validate every create and update against required fields, allowed fields, types, and size limits.
Test rules with emulator scenarios before deploying to shared or production projects.
anti_patterns: Do not use blanket authenticated reads for collections containing private user data.
Do not let owners update documents without schema validation and immutable field checks.
Do not deploy generated rules before reviewing assumptions and query compatibility.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy Firestore automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and command suggestions. Deployment requires local Firebase credentials and explicit user action.

faq.question: Can it generate production-ready Security Rules?
faq.answer: It can create a strong prototype. Production rules still need project review, emulator tests, and launch hardening.

faq.question: Does it support Firestore Standard Edition indexes?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains single-field indexes, composite indexes, and field exemptions for common query patterns.

faq.question: Which SDK does it cover?
faq.answer: The included SDK examples focus on the Firebase Web Modular SDK version 9 or later.

faq.question: Can it help with permission denied errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare the failed operation, authentication state, data shape, and query pattern against the rules.

faq.question: Does it require Firebase CLI?
faq.answer: No. The skill is useful without the CLI, but CLI tools help deploy rules, indexes, and emulator tests.
